projects.name: Cost-of-Carry Futures Arbitrage Backtester
projects.description: A C++ backtesting tool for cash-and-carry arbitrage between the S&P 500 index and E-mini S&P 500 futures using the cost-of-carry pricing model.
projects.overview: This project provides a framework to detect and simulate arbitrage opportunities by comparing actual futures prices against theoretical fair values derived from the cost-of-carry formula. It includes functionality for calculating net profitability, risk metrics, and performing out-of-sample testing and multithreaded grid searches for optimal mispricing thresholds.
features: Calculates theoretical fair value for futures contracts using the cost-of-carry formula.
Simulates cash-and-carry arbitrage trades with configurable notional amounts and transaction costs.
Computes risk metrics including Sharpe ratio and maximum drawdown for backtested strategies.
Supports out-of-sample testing to evaluate strategy robustness and prevent overfitting.
Implements a multithreaded grid search to efficiently test multiple strategy parameters.

evidence.claim: Calculates theoretical fair value for futures contracts using the cost-of-carry formula.
Simulates cash-and-carry arbitrage trades with configurable notional amounts and transaction costs.
Computes risk metrics including Sharpe ratio and maximum drawdown for backtested strategies.
Supports out-of-sample testing to evaluate strategy robustness and prevent overfitting.
Implements a multithreaded grid search to efficiently test multiple strategy parameters.

projects.name: Compiler Construction Project
projects.description: A C-based compiler implementation featuring a DFA-driven lexical analyzer and a predictive parser for a custom programming language.
projects.overview: Developed as part of a Compiler Construction course, this project implements the front-end stages of a compiler. It includes a lexical analyzer that uses a Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) to tokenize source code and a predictive parser that generates a parse tree based on a defined grammar, complete with automated FIRST and FOLLOW set computation.

Automated computation of FIRST and FOLLOW sets for grammar analysis
Predictive parsing to generate a parse tree from a token stream
Command-line driver for executing lexing, parsing, and timing analysis
